newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 1997 economic outlook favourable - fin min.
newsitem.headline: French 1997 economic outlook favourable - fin min.

text.p: France's 1997 economic outlook is favourable, and growth should be fairly robust from the start of the year, a finance ministry official said Thursday.

He had been asked to comment on figures released earlier on Thursday that showed a drop in December consumer spending, highlighting what economists said was weakness in France's economy at the end of last year.
"The overall monetary and financial outlook in Europe is favourable," he told Reuters.

Low interest rates and a rise in the dollar are expected to underpin economic growth this year. The dollar this week rose above 5.50 francs for the first time since 1994 and was trading on Thursday above 5.52 francs.

But the finance ministry official said there would be a rise in household income from the start of the year, due to a reduction in income tax and a decision to allow people to withdraw early 15 billion francs from popular savings schemes (PEPs).
"Overall, from the start of the year, activity should be fairly robust," he said.

Private economists said December's 0.8-percent fall in consumer spending on manufactured goods confirmed that fourth-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) would be weak, meaning the economy will start the year on a soft note.

France needs solid growth this year to meet its target of reducing the budget deficit to three percent of GDP from four percent last year and help tackle unemployment, running at a record 12.7 percent.
The finance ministry official highlighted the fact that consumer spending on manufactured goods had risen an average 3.1 percent over the year, compared to 1.5 percent in 1995.
"There was a real acceleration in consumption," he said.
Full-year consumption figures were compatible with forecasts made in the 1996 budget, he said.
He said one factor that may have affected December data was the fact winter sales did not start until January this year rather than immediately after Christmas.
